title: File Icons Design Rationale
description: Design notes on file-type icons as a carve-out from the general icon rule, including mechanics, the OpenKaava glyph, contrast measurements, and lookup order.
body: File-type icons from VS Code's Material Icon Theme are a deliberate carve-out from the rule that every glyph is hand-authored inline JSX at currentColor. For these icons the colour *is* the information: a tree of fifty rows is scanned by colour, not read — the orange of a .rs against the blue-grey of a .toml is what lets you find the file you want. The carve-out is bounded to file-type icons wherever a filename is listed for someone to scan (Files tree, search overlay), and nowhere else; chrome stays inline SVG at currentColor. Material icons live in public/icons/material/, are generated at build time, and are not in git. OpenKaava's own three icons (.kaava folder and .kaava file) are hand-drawn, live in public/icons/kaava/, and are in git. The icon lookup order: exact filename beats an extension, a longer extension beats a shorter one. Extensions are walked left to right (component.spec.ts tries spec.ts before ts) rather than using only the last segment. The OpenKaava mark is black (#000000) for WCAG contrast (7.66:1 on the amber background), not the light tint the theme convention would use (2.08:1).
